---
title: "GM Session Guide: Chapter 4 (The God's Demand)"
subtitle: "GM guide — Chapter 4"
---

*Vercingetorix named the cult before he was put down at the fort in Session 3. The party now knows what they're looking for: a hidden dungeon in the forest where two of his own chieftains have spent months feeding something they believe is Mars. This session is that dungeon, start to finish.*

**Level:** 5 (marsh) &rarr; 6 (rest of dungeon) &rarr; Advance to 7 at session end · **Players:** 6 (Iris, Julia Jana, Tanit, Rivia, Ursula, Brian) · **Time:** 4-5 hrs · **Type:** Dungeon crawl

---

<div class="session-tree">

<details open>
<summary>📋 Session Quick-Reference — The Whole Session in One Page</summary>

| | |
|---|---|
| **Central question** | What does devotion to a starving god actually produce, once it succeeds? |
| **What must happen** | (1) The party crosses the marsh and clears the Blood Cult Dungeon, room by room. (2) They reach the Core Room and learn what the crystal-star focus actually is and what destroying it will cost. |
| **Player goal** | Cross the marsh, clear the dungeon, defeat the Glabrezu, and learn the shape of Session 5's cost. |
| **Real stakes** | Whether the party recognizes the chieftains' fate as tragedy rather than just another fight. Whether they learn enough in the Core Room to walk into Session 5 prepared rather than surprised. |
| **Session peak moment** | The Gathering Hall: the two chieftains, now Wraiths, turn to face the party in silence for one full round before the fight starts. |
| **Closing image** | The crystal-star focus, examined but unbroken, absorbing every blow thrown at it. The party now knows the name of the place they need to go next. |

**NPCs active this session:**

| NPC | Location at session start | Wants | Role this session |
|---|---|---|---|
| The contubernium (Party) | Entering the Blood Cult Dungeon alone | Clear the cult's sanctum; learn how the spear can be destroyed | Operating behind enemy lines; carries Lucius's locked box |
| The two cult chieftains | Gathering Hall, now Wraiths | Nothing anymore — what's left reacts, not plans | Scene 5's tragic reveal |
| The Glabrezu | Core Room, bound to focus | Guard the crystal tribute anchor | Scene 6 Boss |

**What is NOT in this session:** Legate Corvinus and Augur Cassia stayed at Fort Vindolanda. Centurion Varro and Tribune Lucius are fallen. The old six-day fort siege (Berserkers, Tribal Warriors, Animated Armor, Quintus Flavius) is completely retired.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 0: The Marsh</summary>

Load `SkeletonFortressEntrancePublic.jpg`.

> *The trees thin out and the ground goes soft underfoot before you see why. Ahead, the hillside opens in a mouth -- not a metaphor. A skull carved from the living rock, easily twenty feet across, its eye sockets black even at midday. A causeway of bone and old skulls runs from between its teeth down into a wide, glowing green marsh that splits around the path like water around a stone. The light doesn't flicker like fire. It breathes, slow, the way something alive breathes.*

The bone causeway is the only dry footing. Leaving it means wading through glowing green water.

**Marsh hazard (each round off the causeway):** DC 12 Constitution save or one level of exhaustion and 1 point of temporary corruption. The causeway itself is always safe.

**Two supply caches** at the marsh's near corners. DC 11 Wisdom (Investigation) turns up rations gone green with the same glow, a tally-marked stick counting days, and a torn strip of cloth matching the two chieftains' warband colors.

**Encounter:** 3 × **[Banshee](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16799-banshee)** (*Monster Manual* p. 23 — CR 4, AC 12, HP 58).
- **Environment:** Flanking banshees fly over the marsh; causeway is only 5 ft wide.
- **Actions:** *Corrupting Touch* (+4 to hit, 3d6+2 necrotic), *Horrifying Visage* (DC 13 Wis save or frightened).
- **Wail:** 1/day, DC 13 Con save: drops to 0 HP on failure, or takes 3d6 psychic. Stagger the Wails across rounds; telegraph the scream to create dramatic tension!

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 1: The Ossuary</summary>

Load `Blood-Cult-Dungeon-Gridded-29x43-MapPublic.jpg`, west skull room.

> *The room ahead is round, and its far wall is shaped like the thing you just walked through -- another skull, smaller, teeth picked out in inlaid bone. The floor is a carpet of femurs and ribs, stacked with a care that took someone a long time.*

DC 13 Intelligence (History) (active): the bones are sorted by size, by age, deliberately -- curated for months, not years. Matches the marsh tally-stick.

**Encounter:** 2 × **[Bone Naga](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16812-bone-naga)** (*Monster Manual* p. 233 — CR 4, AC 15, HP 58) + 4 × **[Skeleton](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17015-skeleton)** (*Monster Manual* p. 272 — CR 1/4, AC 13, HP 13).
- **Tactics:** Skeletons have official MM **vulnerability to bludgeoning damage** (maces/warhammers shatter them in 1 hit). Nagas use spellcasting (*hold person*, *ray of sickness*, *ray of enfeeblement*) and Bite (+5, 2d6+3 piercing + 3d6 poison).

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 2: The Blood-Growth Rooms</summary>

Same map, east rooms.

> *The stone here has stopped being stone. Something has grown over it -- clusters of dark red matter, wet-looking, veined, thick as a fist in places and swollen tight. They shift, very slightly, when you get close. Not with the room's air currents.*

DC 12 Wisdom (Medicine) or Intelligence (Nature) (active): organic, fed on blood deliberately and repeatedly, over a long period.

**Encounter:** 1 × **[Yochlol](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17068-yochlol)** (*Monster Manual* p. 65 — CR 6, AC 15, HP 136) + 2 × **[Dretch](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16847-dretch)** (*Monster Manual* p. 57 — CR 1/4, AC 11, HP 18).
- **Yochlol:** Drops in giant spider form (*Shapechanger*), using *Multiattack* (+6, 1d6+3 bludgeoning plus 6d6 poison) and *web*. Magic Resistance.
- **Dretches:** Support chaff. *Fetid Cloud* (1/day, DC 11 Con or retching/poisoned).

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 3: The Minor Altar</summary>

Same map, center room.

> *Four pillars ring a low dais at the room's center, and the dais itself pulses -- not light exactly, more like a heartbeat you can see. This isn't the room you came here looking for. It feels like a rehearsal for one.*

DC 14 Intelligence (Religion) (active): this altar never completed a working -- every mark is a false start. Whatever the cult built up to happened elsewhere.

**Encounter:** 3 × **[Shadow Demon](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17010-shadow-demon)** (*Monster Manual* p. 64 — CR 4, AC 13, HP 66).
- **Official Weaknesses:** Vulnerable to radiant damage; **Light Sensitivity** gives disadvantage on attacks and sight checks in bright light.
- **The Four Braziers:** Lighting the corner braziers illuminates the room, neutralizing *Shadow Stealth* and granting PCs the tactical upper hand.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 4: The Rune Lock</summary>

Same map, south of center.

> *Four tiles are set into the floor here, each etched with a different symbol, each lit from beneath in a different color -- cyan, green, magenta, yellow. There's no door ahead. Whatever this room is guarding, it's guarding it by making you choose.*

**Solution:** cyan &rarr; green &rarr; yellow &rarr; magenta ("beginning, growth, harvest, blood" -- the cult's seasonal liturgy). DC 13 Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Insight) on wear patterns hints at the order.

**Failure:** DC 12 Dexterity save or 2d6 force damage, sequence resets. No lockout, ever. Breather beat.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 5: The Gathering Hall</summary>

Same map, south end.

> *This room was built to hold people. Rows of worn stone mark where dozens once knelt, facing a long table at the far end, still laid with offerings gone black with age. Whatever congregation gathered here, it hasn't gathered in some time. But something is still standing at that table.*

**The reveal:** what's still standing are the two cult chieftains, or what's left of them. DC 13 Wisdom (Insight) before combat identifies torn fragments matching the marsh cache's warband colors.

**Encounter:** 3 × **[Wraith](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/17064-wraith)** (*Monster Manual* p. 302 — CR 5, AC 13, HP 67) -- the two chieftains and their shield-bearer.
- **Round 1:** Recognition, not aggression -- they watch in silence. If spoken to: *"We asked for victory... it took our blood... it starves still..."*
- **Combat:** *Life Drain* (+6, 4d6+3 necrotic, DC 14 Con save vs max HP reduction). *Incorporeal Movement* to glide through stone obstacles.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🎬 Scene 6: The Core Room</summary>

Load `CastleCoreRoomPublic.jpg`.

> *The stair curves up into a perfectly circular chamber. Four stone faces watch from the walls at the compass points -- not gods, not ancestors, just teeth and eyes carved to be looked at from every angle at once. At the center, on a low dais, a crystal the shape of a broken star burns steady and cold. It is the only thing in this entire dungeon that looks cared for.*

**What the crystal actually is:** DC 15 Intelligence (Arcana) or Intelligence (Religion): the cult's real altar and the marsh's source -- tribute funneled here to feed Mars.

**The guardian:** 1 × **[Glabrezu](https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16870-glabrezu)** (*Monster Manual* p. 58 — CR 9, AC 17, HP 157), bound to the focus.
- **Attacks:** Opens with *Darkness*, uses *Power Word Stun* (DC 16 Con) on the primary damage dealer, and attacks with 2 Pincers (+9, 2d10+5 plus grapple DC 15) and 2 Fists (+9, 2d4+5).
- **Pacing:** Against a party of 6 Level 6 characters focusing fire, 157 HP is brought down cleanly in 2-3 fast rounds.

**The Payoff & Rest:** The crystal cannot be destroyed here (Session 5's job). Demonic pressure collapses. The party takes a **Long Rest** in the cleansed Core Room, **advancing to Level 7** with all spell slots and resources refreshed before descending.

</details>

<details>
<summary>🏛️ DM Notes</summary>

**OGAS this session:**
- **The two chieftains (now Wraiths):** Objective: feed the war-god who promised victory. Secret: Mars answered them honestly -- and the cost was everything they were.
- **The Glabrezu:** Objective: protect the crystal-star focus. Secret: pulled into the world by sheer blood tribute, manifesting Mars's hunger.

**Session 4 &rarr; Session 5 handoff:**
- Party enters Session 5 at Level 7 with full HP, spells, and long-rest abilities.
- Party carries Lucius's locked box containing his Germanic childhood mementos and posthumous citizenship recommendations.

</details>
